findings.title: Prod uptime-monitor has not probed since 2026-10-28 21:11Z; stuck in a failing redeploy loop
findings.evidence: Deployment f458bd19 (2026-10-23, commit a28fdc21) logged '[uptime] ok' every 5 min until 2026-10-28 21:11:43Z. That run got 429 x3 from the public URL, then 'curl: (22) ... 429' posting the alert and '[uptime] alert post failed'. After that its status is CRASHED, and logs from 21:12Z to now are empty for the deployment and for the service. Since then 22 deployments (2026-10-28 21:15Z to 2026-10-31 18:00Z, roughly every 4h10m, reason 'redeploy', all of commit c881951f) have FAILED at build with 'failed to fetch snapshot' repeated for 5 min. Later git pushes (8ad4e918, 62f53dec, ...) are SKIPPED by watchPatterns, so nothing replaces the crashed deployment. environment-status: replicaStatus crashed 1, running 0, 'Crashed 3 days ago'.
findings.failure_scenario: Prod has been unmonitored for about 3 days. An outage of the Cloudflare edge, Worker binding or Railway origin (the 2026-07-12 HTTP 523 kind) would page no one through the ERP Uptime topic. The only signal left is the Deployment.failed webhook noise from the loop itself, which trains people to ignore it.
findings.proposed_fix: Owner: deploy uptime-monitor fresh from the current dev commit (e.g. railway up deploy/railway-uptime, or a dashboard deploy of the latest commit), not a redeploy of the c881951f snapshot. Confirm cronSchedule */5 and restartPolicy NEVER are live, and find what keeps re-triggering redeploys every ~4h10m (the audit log shows Deployment.redeployed under the owner's identity; no local crontab or LaunchAgent mentions railway). Add a dead-man check: something outside Railway (the Cloudflare relay's cron) alerts when no 'ok' run has happened in 15 min.
findings.regression_test: Dead-man probe: relay cron reads the last uptime success timestamp (KV written by check.sh on ok) and fires erp_uptime if it is older than 15 min; unit test the age comparison in deploy/railway-alerts.

findings.title: facebook-tracker Postgres password never rotated after the 2026-10-21 Railway env-var breach, and it is on a public TCP proxy
findings.evidence: Audit log 2026-10-19..31 has DatabasePassword.regenerated only for recycle-erp-experiment prod+dev, reddits-tracker, aio and recycle-server-odoo-erp, and none for facebook-tracker. The service's only deployment is 0b89f3e6 from 2026-08-19, and it carries POSTGRES_PASSWORD (name only). The memory note lists 'facebook-tracker DB password (in ~42 homelab containers)' as still pending on 2026-10-23, and nothing has changed since. The proxy is public (syncStatus ACTIVE), so the leaked credential works from anywhere.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever read Railway's customer env vars on 2026-10-21 holds this password. They connect to shortline.proxy.rlwy.net:21141 and read or alter the coordinator database (worker/account state for the Facebook fleet, about 1.19 GB on disk).
findings.proposed_fix: Owner: plan a coordinated rotation. Regenerate in the dashboard, then update the homelab containers' DSN in one batch. Note that updating worker containers means restarts, which are Facebook logins, so do it within a single planned deploy, or first move worker DB access behind rs_console so only the coordinator/console need the new DSN. If the TCP proxy isn't needed, remove it, or restrict it until the rotation is done.
findings.regression_test: After rotation: psql with the old password via the proxy must fail (by fingerprint, no value printed); audit log shows DatabasePassword.regenerated for project ca12c55b.

findings.title: Nightly prod->dev db-sync has failed 4 nights running (scrub nulls a NOT NULL *_enc column); dev frozen at 2026-10-27 and nobody is told
findings.evidence: db-sync logs: 2026-10-28, -29, -30 and -31 at ~04:0xZ each end with 'ERROR: null value in column "url_enc" of relation "fleet_proxies" violates not-null constraint' (CONTEXT 'UPDATE public.fleet_proxies SET url_enc = NULL WHERE url_enc IS NOT NULL'). The last '[sync] done' was 2026-10-27 04:03Z. The generic DO block nulls every column matching _enc$, but 0213 declares url_enc TEXT NOT NULL, and prod gained fleet_proxies rows (row 1, 'NJ1 (Decodo...)', created 2026-10-26). --single-transaction rolls back cleanly, so dev is intact but stale. The deployment stays SUCCESS; environment-status shows only warningCount 1 / state cronReady, and cron-run failures don't emit Deployment.failed, so the railway-alerts webhook never fires.
findings.failure_scenario: Dev, and every e2e/dry-run that relies on 'dev mirrors prod' (data-migration dry runs, the FLEET_ROLE mirror pages), runs on data and schema 4+ days old. A prod migration dry-run passes on dev against the wrong row set, and the gap keeps growing until someone reads the logs.
findings.proposed_fix: In scrub.sql, delete the rows or write a non-null sentinel for NOT NULL *_enc columns (check a.attnotnull in the loop: DELETE FROM the table, or SET col = '' / a dev-sealed placeholder), and handle fleet_proxies explicitly. Make sync.sh's failure visible: post to the relay /alert (topic e.g. erp_dbsync) on any non-zero exit.
findings.regression_test: Repro: migrate a scratch DB, insert one fleet_proxies row with url_enc set, then run scrub.sql with psql ON_ERROR_STOP=1. It must succeed and leave no non-null url_enc; currently it errors with 23502.

findings.title: [cross-lane] Cloudflare answered 429 to the Railway uptime probe, for both the app and the alert relay, while origin was 200
findings.location: railway:uptime-monitor deployment f458bd19-04b6-417d-901c-1943ff492510 logs 2026-10-28T21:11Z; backend http log 2026-10-28T21:11:39Z /api/health 200 from 152.55.181.187
findings.evidence: inventory.recycleservers.com/api/health returned 429 three times 20 s apart. The origin probe in the same run got 200 (seen in the backend http log). The POST to ALERT_URL (the railway-alerts relay) also got 429. The relay code (deploy/railway-alerts/worker.js) never returns 429; it only returns 204/401/400/404/502. So the 429s came from Cloudflare's edge, plausibly a rate or bot rule keyed on Railway's shared egress IP. The backend's own 429 paths (oauth, scan, me, publicForms) don't cover /api/health.
findings.failure_scenario: The probe reports a false 'prod DOWN (edge layer)'. When the edge really throttles Railway egress, the alert that would report it is throttled by the same edge, so a genuine outage goes unreported. It also triggered the crash in B1-01.
findings.proposed_fix: Cloudflare lane: exempt /api/health and the relay /alert from rate/bot rules for this probe (custom header or a WAF skip rule), or probe from somewhere other than Railway. In check.sh, treat 429 as 'probe throttled', distinct from DOWN.
findings.regression_test: check.sh against a fake endpoint returning 429: it should classify the result as throttled, not as an edge outage.

findings.title: Prod backend watchPatterns omit package.json / pnpm-lock.yaml / tsconfig.base.json that dev has
findings.evidence: Prod watchPatterns are ['apps/backend/**','packages/shared/**']. Dev watchPatterns for the same service are ['apps/backend/**','packages/shared/**','package.json','pnpm-lock.yaml','tsconfig.base.json'].
findings.failure_scenario: A release whose backend-relevant change is only in the lockfile (e.g. a pnpm audit fix of a transitive backend dependency) or the root tsconfig merges to main. Dev rebuilds, prod is SKIPPED and keeps running the vulnerable or old dependency tree, and nothing shows it. The same happens to the root version bump: prod /api/health keeps reporting an older version than main.
findings.proposed_fix: Set prod watchPatterns equal to dev's, ideally through config-as-code (a railway.toml for the backend, so the two environments can't drift).
findings.regression_test: Compare get-service-config watchPatterns for both environments in a CI or ops script; fail on difference.

findings.title: Vaultwarden (password.jinhu.us) volume has no backups recorded
findings.evidence: Audit log 2026-10-19..31: Backup.created events exist for recycle-erp-experiment (11), aio (12) and recycle-server-odoo-erp (13), and none for vaultwarden. The project has one service and no backup job. Image vaultwarden/server:1.37.1, deployed once on 2026-10-13. Variables include SIGNUPS_ALLOWED; its value was not read.
findings.failure_scenario: A volume loss or corruption, or a bad image upgrade, destroys the password vault with no restore point. If SIGNUPS_ALLOWED is true, anyone on the internet can also register an account on it.
findings.proposed_fix: Owner: enable Railway volume backups on the vaultwarden volume, or add an encrypted export to R2. Confirm that SIGNUPS_ALLOWED is false and that an ADMIN_TOKEN policy is intended.
findings.regression_test: Audit log shows Backup.created for project 1f5ba707 daily.

findings.title: Next-task long-polls and VNC sockets error on every prod deploy
findings.evidence: In the 7-day window: 538 5xx out of 465,949 requests (0.115%). Since 2026-10-28, every 5xx is a burst at a deploy (15:23Z, 18:55Z on 10-31): about 20 x 503 on /api/fleet/worker/vnc in 2 ms, and 502 on /api/fleet/worker/next-task after 35-44 s ('connection closed unexpectedly'). next-task holds poll_hold_seconds (p50 = 30000 ms), while shutdown closes connections at graceMs 20 s. The 30000 ms p95 seen on the backend comes entirely from these holds; interactive paths are fine (/api/inventory p95 48 ms).
findings.failure_scenario: Each release gives fleet workers a 502 and drops VNC viewers. That is harmless only as long as the clients keep retrying. Any latency or error alert built on the service-wide p95 or 5xx rate will be noise.
findings.proposed_fix: On SIGTERM, answer held next-task polls immediately with 'nothing_due' (wake every hold) before server.close. Exclude long-poll paths from any latency alert.
findings.regression_test: Backend test: with a held next-task, calling the shutdown hook resolves the request with a 200 nothing_due within 1 s.

findings.title: Prod-environment uptime-monitor builds from branch dev, with no release gate
findings.evidence: get-service-config production: source {branch: 'dev', rootDirectory: 'deploy/railway-uptime'}. Prod backend and pg-r2-backup track main.
findings.failure_scenario: A change to check.sh merged to dev reaches the prod probe immediately, before the dev->main release review, and could silence prod monitoring with no release.
findings.proposed_fix: Point the production uptime-monitor at main, or document why dev is intended.

findings.title: Reddit tracker deploys carry no commit, healthcheck or draining window
findings.evidence: Deployments 1ca1fcad and 5e40e87b (2026-10-31 09:15Z) have meta {reason: 'deploy'} with no commitHash (railway up uploads), so the running code can't be compared with dev 62f53dec or main fb4afda4. describe-service shows no healthcheckPath and no drainingSeconds on api. Health in the last 7 days is good: 1,081 requests, 0 5xx, p95 <= 290 ms, worker RAM about 0.12 GB.
findings.failure_scenario: After an incident, nobody can tell which tracker commit was live. A broken api deploy goes live with no healthcheck to stop it.
findings.proposed_fix: Record the git SHA in an env/var or log line at deploy time (deploy script sets GIT_SHA). Set healthcheckPath=/health on the api service via a service-level override, since the shared railway.toml can't carry one.

findings.title: Backend variable names drift from env.ts
findings.evidence: Set on Railway but never read by apps/packages/deploy: FLEET_IMAGE_AGENT (prod and dev); ADMIN_PASSWORD, read only by scripts/init-admin.mjs, so it is a standing admin secret in the runtime env. Read by code but absent on both environments: COORDINATOR_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID/_SECRET (root AGENTS.md lists them as contract env; optional in routes/coordinator.ts:39-44, and coordinator traffic shows no 5xx since 10-28, so Access is evidently not enforced). Dev sets FLEET_ROLE but no FLEET_MIRROR_URL/_CLIENT_ID/_SECRET, so fleet/mirror.ts:20-21 forwardsReads() is false and dev's mirror pages read the local copy, which B1-03 has frozen at 10-27. Prod lacks MAIL_* (mail dark on prod) and dev lacks MERCURY/PAYPAL/SHIPPO (stubs), which looks intended. Reddit api/worker names match trackers/reddit/src (TELEGRAM_API_ID/HASH/USER_SESSION are read in config.ts:81).
findings.failure_scenario: A leftover ADMIN_PASSWORD widens what a future env-var leak exposes. The AGENTS.md contract table misleads whoever debugs a coordinator 403. Dev fleet pages silently show stale data.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove FLEET_IMAGE_AGENT and (after confirming init-admin isn't run at boot) ADMIN_PASSWORD from the runtime env. Either set the FLEET_MIRROR_* trio on dev or document local-copy mode. Mark COORDINATOR_ACCESS_* optional in AGENTS.md.
